bundle.guidance:
# Software Manual

Operating documentation for the administrators who install, configure and
recover a system. The reader is usually mid-incident, following along at a
keyboard. Every page answers "what do I type next".

## Principles

1. **Procedures are numbered, always.** A task is an ordered list of steps
   with one action per step. Prose that hides a step inside a paragraph is a
   defect.
2. **State the precondition before the first step.** Permissions, version,
   environment. A reader who cannot complete step one has wasted the page.
3. **Show the expected result.** Each procedure ends with how to verify it
   worked, not with the last command.

## Layout grid

Single column at `max-width: 48rem`. `--space-xl` between tasks,
`--space-lg` between a task heading and its first step. Callouts and step
tables run the full column width. Do not nest procedures more than one level;
a sub-procedure becomes its own task with a cross-reference.

## Typography

One family throughout (IBM Plex Sans) at `--size-h1` / `--size-h2` /
`--size-h3`; hierarchy comes from weight and spacing, not from a second
typeface. Commands, paths, file names and values are always monospace
(`--font-family-mono`), inline as well as in blocks. Never paraphrase a
literal string — quote it exactly.

## Colour usage

Teal (`--color-brand-primary`) marks step numbers, links and the `tip` callout
rule. Status colours are reserved for callouts: `ok` for tips, `warn` for
cautions, `danger` for anything that can lose data or lock an account. Body
text stays `--color-text-primary` on white; cards use `--color-bg-card`. Never
colour-code steps themselves.

## Charts

Chart.js only for capacity and sizing guidance — bar or line, two series
maximum, with the axis units spelled out. Operational documentation rarely
needs a chart; a table of thresholds is usually the honest form.

## Diagrams

Mermaid `flowchart TD` for decision trees ("is the service reachable?") and
`sequenceDiagram` for multi-component handshakes. Label every edge on a
decision tree with the literal condition.

## Components and when to use each

- `procedure` — the numbered task itself. Every "how do I…" section is one.
- `callout` — note, tip, caution or danger. Use `danger` only for
  irreversible actions; overuse destroys its meaning.
- `step-table` — parameters or values a step needs, or a matrix of settings
  per environment. Use when a step would otherwise carry four or more values.
- `prereq-box` — the preconditions block above a procedure.
- `cli` — a labelled command with its expected output.

## Do / don't

- **Do** write steps in the imperative: "Run", "Select", "Confirm".
- **Do** give the rollback for anything destructive, in the same task.
- **Don't** say "simply", "just" or "obviously".
- **Don't** describe the UI position of a control ("the blue button top
  right") — name the control.
- **Don't** mix versions in one procedure; branch into two tasks instead.

components.name: procedure
components.description: A numbered task: ordered steps with one action each.
components.when_to_use: Every 'how do I...' section. Always numbered, always with a verification step.
components.html:
1. Stop the service: systemctl stop hub
  2. Back up the configuration directory.
  3. Apply the new release and restart.
  4. Verify: curl -fsS localhost:8000/health returns 200.

components.name: callout
components.description: Note, tip, caution or danger box.
components.when_to_use: Danger only for irreversible actions; caution for anything needing a rollback plan.
components.html:
Danger

Purging the trash deletes every version permanently. There is no undo.
